faq: Does it work with Gmail and Outlook?
Yes. Gmail, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 or Outlook are the usual cases, and most CRMs connect to them. Tell us which provider you use and we check that your CRM supports it before we start.
Will the CRM see all my personal email?
No. We set the sync to log only emails with people in your CRM, and you can choose to keep other messages out. Each user approves their own connection, so nobody is connected without knowing.
Open tracking is optional and set up only on request in Premium. Some countries require notice for tracking, so we recommend telling contacts, and we follow your CRM's own rules for it.
Do I need a paid CRM plan?
Some CRMs limit email sync to paid plans. We check this at the start and tell you which plan you need. The plan fee goes to the CRM company, and our price covers the connection work.

desc:
CRM email sync and inbox connection saves every email you send and receive on the matching contact and deal. Ecom Swift LLC connects your team's inboxes to your CRM, sets who can see what and tests it with real messages before you rely on it.

## What does CRM email sync do?

CRM email sync links a mailbox to your customer records. When you write to a lead or they write to you, the message is stored on that contact's timeline and, where relevant, on their open deal. Nobody has to copy, paste or forward anything.

The result is one shared history. A colleague who picks up a conversation can read what was already said, instead of asking the customer to repeat themselves.

## The problem with email living in private inboxes

Most selling happens in email, yet most CRMs only see what someone remembers to type in. A quote sent from a personal inbox, a reply buried in a thread and a question answered by a colleague all stay invisible. When that person is away or leaves, the history goes with them.

This causes small but costly failures: a follow-up sent twice, a promise forgotten, a manager who cannot tell whether a deal is alive or stuck. Connecting the inbox closes that gap without asking people to change how they write.

## How synced email improves sales follow-up

Logged conversations give your reminders and reports something real to work with. A task such as "contact again in three days" makes sense only if the CRM knows when the last message went out. Dashboards that show activity per deal depend on the same record.

Sync also speeds up daily work. Templates stored in the CRM let a salesperson send a consistent first reply in moments. Optional open and click tracking tells them when a quote was viewed, so a call can be timed sensibly. Used with care, it makes follow-up more relevant rather than more frequent.

## What a well-run email connection includes

- Each chosen inbox connected through the account's own sign-in, never through shared passwords.
- Sent and received messages matched to existing contacts and deals.
- Sharing rules that decide who sees full messages, who sees only subject lines and who sees none.
- A way to keep personal or sensitive threads out of the CRM altogether.
- A shared sales inbox where several people answer the same address.
- Shared templates for the replies your team writes most often.
- Open and click tracking switched on only where you want it.
- A review of messages that did not match any contact.
- Calendar linking, where your package covers it, so meetings appear on the record.

## How we set it up

We begin with a short call or message to learn who uses which inbox and what each person is comfortable sharing. Then we connect the inboxes inside your CRM settings, choose the visibility rules and send test emails in both directions. We check that a message to a known contact lands on the right record and that an unknown sender behaves the way you expect.

The Basic package covers a single inbox. Standard adds more inboxes, visibility rules per user and shared templates. Premium extends to a larger team, a shared sales inbox and a review of unmatched mail once the system has run for a while. You also receive a short guide on adding the CRM address to cc or bcc for situations where automatic sync is not enough.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Agree with each user what the CRM may see before connecting their mailbox.
- Tell the team the sync exists, so nobody is surprised.
- Use shared templates for repeat replies and keep them short.
- Turn tracking on only for emails where it helps you.
- Check the unmatched list in the first weeks.

**Avoid:**
- Syncing a personal mailbox without the owner's clear consent.
- Giving every user full visibility by default.
- Treating open tracking as proof that someone read or agreed to anything.
- Connecting an inbox that mixes private life and work without filters.
- Leaving the connection running after an employee leaves.

## Who this service is for

It suits a small sales team that currently forwards important emails to a colleague "for the record." It suits a founder who handles most conversations alone and wants a trail before hiring the first salesperson. And it suits a service business where several people answer one info address and need to see who replied to whom.

## What we need from you

Tell us which inboxes to connect and which provider each one uses, such as Gmail or Outlook. Each user authorizes the connection from their own account, or you add us as an admin of the CRM so we can guide it. We never need your email password. Please also tell us who may see what, any domains or contacts to exclude, and whether you want tracking. Your CRM plan decides which email features are available, so we check that first and tell you plainly if something needs a different plan.
